CLKCTRLGeneric Clock Controlp. 100

offset 0x2 · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W

  • Configures the generic clock named in CLKCTRL.ID. Write it as one 16-bit access holding the settings and the ID; to read one clock's settings, first write its ID to CLKCTRL.ID with an 8-bit access, then read the register.
  • A power reset resets CLKCTRL for every ID, the RTC's included. A user reset resets it only for IDs other than the RTC whose WRTLOCK is 0.
  • After a power reset: WDT has GEN 0x02, and CLKEN and WRTLOCK each follow the WDT Enable and WDT Always-On bits of the NVM User Row (1 if written to one, 0 if to zero); RTC and all others reset to 0x00 in all three fields.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
15WRTLOCKR/W0Writing it locks against further writes the generic clock named by CLKCTRL.ID, the generator named by CLKCTRL.GEN and that generator's division factor; only a power reset unlocks them. Generator 0 can never be locked.
0Generic clock, its generator and division factor unlocked.
1Generic clock, its generator and division factor locked.
14CLKENR/W0Turns the generic clock on or off.
0Generic clock off.
1Generic clock on.
11:8GENR/W0x0Generator feeding this generic clock: 0x0 GCLK0, 0x1 GCLK1, 0x2 GCLK2, 0x3 GCLK3, 0x4 GCLK4, 0x5 GCLK5 (generic clock generators 0 to 5); 0x6-0xF reserved.
0x0GCLK0Clock generator 0.
0x1GCLK1Clock generator 1.
0x2GCLK2Clock generator 2.
0x3GCLK3Clock generator 3.
0x4GCLK4Clock generator 4.
0x5GCLK5Clock generator 5.
0x6-0xFReserved.
5:0IDR/W0x0Picks which generic clock this CLKCTRL access configures. A power reset resets CLKCTRL for every ID, RTC included; a user reset resets it for an ID other than RTC whose WRTLOCK is 0. After a power reset GEN, CLKEN and WRTLOCK read 0 for every ID except WDT, whose GEN is 0x02 and whose CLKEN and WRTLOCK are 1 when the NVM User Row WDT Enable and WDT Always-On bits are 1, 0 when they are 0. After a user reset: RTC's GEN and CLKEN go to 0 only if WRTLOCK and CLKEN are both 0, otherwise unchanged, and its WRTLOCK is unchanged; WDT's GEN goes to 0x02 and its CLKEN follows the User Row WDT Enable bit if WRTLOCK is 0, otherwise both unchanged, and its WRTLOCK is unchanged; for other IDs GEN and CLKEN go to 0 if WRTLOCK is 0, otherwise unchanged.

GENCTRLGeneric Clock Generator Controlp. 103

offset 0x4 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W

  • Configures the generator named in GENCTRL.ID. Write it as one 32-bit access holding the settings and the ID; to read one generator's settings, first write its ID to GENCTRL.ID with an 8-bit access, then read the register.
  • A power reset resets GENCTRL for every ID, the RTC's generator included. A user reset returns generator 0 to its power-reset value, and every other generator too unless it is a source of the RTC clock or of a locked generic clock; such a generator keeps its value.
  • Reset values by generator ID: 0x00 0x00010600, 0x01 0x00000001, 0x02 0x00010302, 0x03 0x00000003, 0x04 0x00000004, 0x05 0x00000005.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
21RUNSTDBYR/W0Keeps the generator running in standby when it is set to drive its GCLK_IO pin. With GENCTRL.OE at 0 it has no effect, and the generator runs only when a peripheral asks for its clock.
0Generator stops in standby; GCLK_IO sits at the level GENCTRL.OOV sets.
1Generator keeps running in standby and drives its GCLK_IO pin.
20DIVSELR/W0Chooses how the generator divides its clock source. For an undivided source, DIVSEL must be 0 and the generator's GENDIV.DIV must be 0 or 1.
0Output is the source divided by GENDIV.DIV.
1Output is the source divided by 2^(GENDIV.DIV+1).
19OER/W0Sends the generated clock out on GCLK_IO, when GCLK_IO is not chosen as a source in GENCLK.SRC.
0Generator not sent out.
1Generator sent out on its GCLK_IO, unless that GCLK_IO is chosen as a source in GENCLK.SRC.
18OOVR/W0Level driven on the GCLK_IO pin whenever that pin is not picked as a source in GENCLK.SRC.
0GCLK_IO is 0 while the generator is off or OE is 0.
1GCLK_IO is 1 while the generator is off or OE is 0.
17IDCR/W0Evens out the generator's duty cycle for odd division factors.
0Duty cycle not 50/50 with odd division factors.
1Duty cycle 50/50.
16GENENR/W0Turns the generic clock generator on or off.
0Generator off.
1Generator on.

CTRLAControl Ap. 365

offset 0x00 · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
15:8CMDEXR/W0x0Key that lets the command in CMD run: 0xA5 executes it; any other key blocks the write and sets STATUS.PROGE, as does a write while an earlier command is still running. Write it together with CMD, and only while READY is 1. An APB command arriving in the same cycle as an AHB access waits until the AHB access and the NVM block are idle. Bit 0 reads 1 until the command has been issued. 0xA5: KEY, execution key; 0x00-0xA4 and 0xA6-0xFF: reserved.
0x0-0xa4Reserved.
0xA5KEYExecution key.
0xa6-0xffReserved.
6:0CMDR/W0x0Command that runs when the CMDEX key is written alongside it.
0x0-0x1Reserved.
0x2ERErase row: erases the row at the address in ADDR.
0x3Reserved.
0x4WPWrite page: writes the page buffer into the page at the address in ADDR.
0x5EARErase auxiliary row: erases the auxiliary row at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear and only for the user configuration row.
0x6WAPWrite auxiliary page: writes the page buffer into the auxiliary page at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear and only for the user configuration row.
0x7-0x9Reserved.
0xASFSF: security flow command.
0xb-0xeReserved.
0xFWLWL: write the lockbits.
0x10-0x3fReserved.
0x40LRLock region: locks the region holding the address in ADDR.
0x41URUnlock region: unlocks the region holding the address in ADDR.
0x42SPRMSPRM: set power reduction mode.
0x43CPRMCPRM: clear power reduction mode.
0x44PBCPBC: clear the page buffer.
0x45SSBSet security bit: writes 0x00 into the first byte of the lockbit row, which sets the security bit.
0x46INVALLINVALL: invalidate every cache line.

17:16READMODER/W0x0How the cache handles misses. 0x0 NO_MISS_PENALTY: no wait state added on a miss; highest system performance. 0x1 LOW_POWER: the cache uses less power but adds a wait state on every miss, stalling the CPU and possibly lengthening run time. 0x2 DETERMINISTIC: a hit and a miss take the same time, set by the programmed flash wait states, for real-time code needing fixed timing. 0x3: reserved.
0x0NO_MISS_PENALTYNo wait state on a cache miss; best system performance.

SCL is released and MB clears on a write to ADDR.ADDR, a write to DATA.DATA, a read of DATA.DATA with CTRLB.SMEN on, or a valid write to CTRLB.CMD. Writing 1 clears MB, but the transaction neither goes on nor ends until one of those actions happens. Writing 0 does nothing.

10:0ADDRR/W0x0Writing the address starts an action chosen by the bus state. Unknown: the operation stops, with INTFLAG.MB and STATUS.BUSERR set. Busy: the master waits for the bus to go idle. Idle: the master sends a START and the address; on an ACK, SCL is held low and both STATUS.CLKHOLD and INTFLAG.MB set. Owner: a repeated START is sent, preceded by the acknowledge action if the last transfer was a read; this write is made while either INTFLAG.MB or INTFLAG.SB is 1. The whole address is sent whether arbitration is won or lost; after a loss, ones are sent for the rest of it. A write clears INTFLAG.MB, INTFLAG.SB, STATUS.ARBLOST and STATUS.BUSERR. Reading it any time leaves the bus alone. Bit 0 is the R/W bit: 0 write, 1 read.
